ordinance

OR-dih-nunts — an ordinance puts things in proper order; careful not to confuse it with 'ordnance' (military weapons), which has no 'i.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ordinance is an authoritative order or regulation, especially one passed by a local government.

The city passed a new ordinance requiring all restaurants to post their health inspection scores in the front window.

Example

Residents of a small town keep complaining about stray dogs running loose in the park. After months of debate, the town council formally passes an ordinance requiring every dog owner to keep their pet on a leash in public, with fines for anyone who doesn't comply.

That formal, official rule passed by a local government to solve a specific problem is what makes it an ordinance. Unlike 'suggestion,' which anyone can ignore, an ordinance is a binding, authoritative order.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

regulation: A regulation is an official rule made by an authority — often an agency spelling out details, like safety codes or food-handling rules. An ordinance is the local law itself, debated and passed by a city or town council rather than issued by an agency.

decree: A decree is an official order handed down by a single ruler or authority — one person announces it, and it carries the force of law. An ordinance is enacted the opposite way: a local council debates it and votes it into effect.

bylaw: A bylaw is a rule an organization makes for its own members — a club, a homeowners' association, a company board. An ordinance binds everyone in a town or city, because it comes from the local government, not a private group.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

suggestion: an idea offered for consideration, not required

recommendation: advice about what should be done, without requiring it

Where it sits · how high the authority behind it is — rule → ordinance → statute

rule vs. ordinance: Rule is a more general, weaker word than ordinance — a rule can be made by anyone, even informally, while an ordinance is specifically an official law passed by a local government.

statute vs. ordinance: Statute can feel even weightier than ordinance: an ordinance is usually passed by a city or county, but a statute is a formal law passed by a state or national legislature.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — -ordin-

root — -ordin-: order, arrangement (Latin (ordo))

suffix — -ance

suffix — -ance: state or act of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin ordinare meant 'to arrange, to put in order,' from ordo, 'order, row.' An ordinance, at its root, is an official act of putting a rule properly in order for everyone to follow.

Use the root in a new word: coordinate

Use the root in a new word: coordinate: Their manager spent all morning on the phone, coordinating with the branch office.
